items.title: Binance tries to recover $6.3 billion stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.summary: Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, is attempting to recover about $6.3 billion taken in a cyber-attack believed to be the largest of its kind. Blockchain intelligence firms have linked the hack to North Korea, and the exchange is working to freeze the funds. One report says the theft took about 20 minutes.

items.title: Trade unions march in Port-of-Spain; PM calls protest a 'bust'
items.summary: Trade union members, joined by opposition parties, marched from Memorial Park to Woodford Square to press the Government on pay and working conditions. Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar called the protest a 'bust' and told participants to return to work Monday, while two government ministers also criticized it.

items.title: PowerGen workers to receive $66.1 million wage settlement
items.summary: About 150 PowerGen workers will receive overdue salary payments before Christmas after negotiations concluded on a $66.1 million wage settlement. Public Utilities Minister Barry Padarath made the announcement in Parliament.

items.title: Divali Nagar opens to modest crowds amid funding controversy
items.summary: The Divali Nagar opened to the public with a relatively modest turnout in its first hours, with several booths still being set up. The opening comes amid a funding controversy.

items.title: T&T government defends stance on Cuba embargo at the UN
items.summary: Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar and Foreign Affairs Minister Sean Sobers defended Trinidad and Tobago's vote against a UN resolution on the US embargo of Cuba. Sobers said the decision was not a vote against the Cuban people but in support of their right to democracy.

items.title: Imbert says proposed cannabis law changes infringe on religious freedom
items.summary: Opposition MP Colm Imbert argued that proposed changes to cannabis laws would infringe on religious freedom and privacy, accusing the Government of being anti-religion, anti-Catholic Church and anti-Rastafarian.

items.title: Marcelle denies family link to TSTT arson suspects
items.summary: Laventille West MP Kareem Marcelle denied claims that a relative was among those arrested over the suspected arson attack at a TSTT compound in Laventille.

items.title: Global nature talks reach a deal, with funding still unresolved
items.summary: Countries at global nature talks reached a deal as they try to get an agreement to halt nature decline back on track. Money remains an issue.

items.title: Police deployed in stand-off over control of Poland's top court
items.summary: Police were deployed during a stand-off over control of a top Polish court. The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.

items.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.summary: The United States has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine. The American-made interceptors are described as the only effective weapon for downing Russia's ballistic missiles.

items.title: NASA seeks industry ideas for servicing the Hubble telescope
items.summary: NASA issued a Request for Information on Oct. 29 to learn about industry capabilities for in-space servicing of the Hubble Space Telescope. The agency solicited ideas for reboosting Hubble four years ago, but they did not go anywhere.

items.title: Xavier Becerra outlines day-one priorities if elected governor
items.summary: Democrat Xavier Becerra walked through his day-one priorities if elected governor of California.

items.title: Two San Francisco tech companies cut more than 100 jobs
items.summary: Two San Francisco tech companies have cut more than 100 jobs.

items.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to a third US state
items.summary: Screwworms have spread to a third US state and are attacking pets. The USDA has identified 74 animal cases in the US since the parasitic flies arrived in June.

items.title: Suspect in fatal SF scooter hit-and-run arrested in San Rafael
items.summary: A driver suspected in a fatal scooter hit-and-run in San Francisco was arrested in San Rafael.

items.title: Patrick Stewart remembered for his role as Jean-Luc Picard
items.summary: Writers at Ars Technica and elsewhere are remembering Patrick Stewart, particularly for his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. Stewart once said that for huge numbers of people he would always be Picard.

items.title: SF startup behind robot-dog walker ad reports visit and threats from resident
items.summary: A San Francisco startup behind a 'Robot-Dog Walkers Wanted' ad received a visit and threatening texts from an angry resident.

items.title: G20 family photo cancelled after protests over Russian minister's presence
items.summary: A G20 'family photo' was cancelled after protests over the presence of a Russian minister. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted his Russian counterpart at the meeting and accused his government of killing innocent civilians in Ukraine.

items.title: Boom shifts toward powering AI data centers, putting supersonic airliner in doubt
items.summary: Boom's supersonic airliner may be delayed as the company shifts to powering AI data centers. Its data center power business has also lost a customer.

items.title: Lawmakers and drivers press California regulators on autonomous vehicles
items.summary: Ride-hail workers and local officials called on the California Public Utilities Commission to put driverless car regulation in the hands of local leaders.

items.title: Anthropic VS Code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
items.summary: An Anthropic VS Code extension on Cursor was backdoored for nearly 12 hours. It is still unknown how attackers gained access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.

items.title: Newsom has until Monday to decide on $1.42 billion in federal broadband money
items.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom must decide by Monday whether California accepts $1.42 billion in federal broadband funding. The money comes with a provision that would bar the state from enforcing many of its own consumer protection rules for about 14 years, a choice KQED describes as a key wildfire safety decision.

items.title: Novaya Gazeta shut under pressure from Russian authorities
items.summary: The founder of Novaya Gazeta said authorities 'strangled' the newspaper after it was shut under official pressure. It has been one of Russia's most high-profile independent news outlets for the past three decades.

items.title: Dartmouth provost loses job over his own AI use
items.summary: Dartmouth's provost, who had warned about AI cheating, lost his job because of his own use of AI.

items.title: US tech stocks fall sharply as AI spending nears $1 trillion
items.summary: US tech stocks fell sharply, with the Nasdaq opening at its lowest level in more than two months and Intel shares continuing to drop. Fears over AI spending, which is nearing $1 trillion, also triggered a large one-day loss for Google shares.

items.title: Study finds more than 25% of people lie to get antibiotics
items.summary: More than a quarter of people lie to obtain antibiotics, according to a report. The faked symptoms still point to infections that antibiotics do not treat.

items.title: Advocates defend noncitizen voting in SF school board races
items.summary: San Francisco granted noncitizen parents the right to vote in local school board elections ten years ago. Advocates worry eligible voters are being intimidated by the Trump administration as it targets voter rolls.

items.title: Disappearing old ice is revealing Stone Age material
items.summary: An article reports that the oldest ice is disappearing and that traces of the Stone Age are emerging from it.

items.title: Few customers are using AI agents for DoorDash orders
items.summary: Almost no one is using AI agents to place DoorDash orders, though the e-commerce use case is still relatively new.

items.title: DOJ subpoenas California election officials despite judge's warning
items.summary: Federal prosecutors subpoenaed California election officials after a federal judge warned them to stop threatening those officials.

items.title: Study dates meteorite Teghaza 001 as one of the oldest pieces of Mars found
items.summary: A NASA-funded study found that Teghaza 001, a rose-colored meteorite of nearly 2 pounds found in the Sahara in 2022, formed on Mars more than 4.1 billion years ago. The rock is a rare piece of the planet's ancient crust, and scientists identified 13 Martian locations that match its mineralogy and chemistry.

items.title: Early voting and ballot drop-off options open across the Bay Area
items.summary: Early voting is available across the Bay Area this weekend, and KQED has published guides to finding polling places and ballot drop boxes. The guides also cover envelope signatures and how to correct ballot mistakes.

items.title: Fujifilm to increase tape production fivefold on AI archiving demand
items.summary: Fujifilm plans to boost magnetic tape production five times as AI drives demand for archiving. Tape offers low costs and offline security.

items.title: Christa Pike describes surviving failed execution attempt
items.summary: US inmate Christa Pike said she woke up 'confused and in pain' after a failed execution. It is her first public statement since she survived a lethal injection attempt in September.

items.title: Canada ends avalanche dog rescue programme in Rocky Mountains
items.summary: Canada has ended a 55-year-old dog rescue programme in the Rocky Mountains as part of government budget cuts. The programme has found missing hikers and children in the wilderness, and the decision has drawn outrage.

items.title: DOJ says thousands of 'ghost students' used AI to steal millions in student loans
items.summary: The US Justice Department says thousands of so-called ghost students used AI to steal millions of dollars in student loans. The crackdown may complicate applying for FAFSA.

items.title: Latino voters weigh choices in Southern California swing district
items.summary: Latino voters in California's 58th Assembly District swung for Trump in 2024 and might flip again.

items.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during ceasefire
items.summary: Hundreds of people were evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky during a rare ceasefire in the Ukraine war. Hundreds more are understood to have stayed in the front-line town.

items.title: Analysts say looming satellite launch crisis is worse than anticipated
items.summary: Analysts found that a looming launch crisis is more severe than previously anticipated. There is no evidence that Starship will launch traditional satellites.

items.title: Witnesses testify in bribery trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao
items.summary: Mario Juarez, who has pleaded guilty to participating in the alleged bribery scheme involving Thao and three others, took the stand. Former Oakland employee LaTonda Simmons testified Thursday about going to the Justice Department with her suspicions, alleging a far-reaching conspiracy.

items.title: Webb telescope images the Cat's Head Nebula
items.summary: NASA released a mid-infrared view of the Cat's Head Nebula from the James Webb Space Telescope on Oct. 29. The nebula's shape was likely sculpted over time by intense ultraviolet radiation.

items.title: US senator links Egypt press crackdown to military aid decision
items.summary: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on US military aid to Egypt paved the way for arrests of journalists there.

items.title: Northflank reported breached
items.summary: A report shared on Hacker News says Northflank was breached.

items.title: Vatican hosts dialogue on AI and human dignity
items.summary: The Vatican hosted a dialogue on artificial intelligence and human dignity.

items.title: Spanish transport minister refuses to resign after high-speed train collision
items.summary: Transport Minister Oscar Puente said he will not resign after two high-speed trains collided earlier in the week, killing at least 69 people when one struck the other from behind. It is Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year and comes ahead of a national election.

items.title: 3D maps show the interstellar medium is dynamic, not static
items.summary: Astronomers long treated the interstellar medium as a static backdrop. A wave of 3D mapping is now bringing its dynamic nature into focus.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
items.summary: The Chicago-born pope mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.

items.title: GM to pay $220 million over sale of Smart Driver data
items.summary: General Motors will pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data. Owners of GM cars found their driving data had been sold to insurance companies.

items.title: Energy takes 72% of T&T state company investment budget
items.summary: Energy accounts for 72% of Trinidad and Tobago's state company investment budget.

items.title: BART service resumes through Transbay Tube after equipment issue
items.summary: BART service through the Transbay Tube has resumed after an equipment issue.

items.title: Researcher builds quantum system of 24,000 atoms to study the origin of time
items.summary: A University of Birmingham researcher used 24,000 ultracold atoms to build an isolated quantum system described as a miniature universe. The work is intended to help address what time is and where it comes from.

items.title: Warm tropical refuges may explain how crocodiles survived the dinosaur extinction
items.summary: An analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs because their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable.

items.title: CNOOC hopeful of securing T&T deep-sea projects
items.summary: China's CNOOC is hopeful of securing deep-sea projects in Trinidad and Tobago.

items.title: Musk and Zuckerberg echo Trump's 'super intelligence' branding on earnings calls
items.summary: Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg echoed President Trump's push to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' on earnings calls, while other executives did not.

items.title: Alaska governor orders probe into spoiler candidate claims; Hegseth ousts Army general
items.summary: Alaska's governor ordered an investigation into claims that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate in the state's Senate race. Separately, Hegseth ousted an Army general as the US prepares for potential attacks on Iran.

items.title: Hubble finding challenges explanation of how early universe cleared
items.summary: Observations from the Hubble Space Telescope are challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago. Scientists had believed winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape.

items.title: Study estimates snakebites kill 274,000 to 513,000 people a year
items.summary: A new study estimates that venomous snakebites kill 274,000 to 513,000 people worldwide each year, far more than official statistics indicate. As many as 7 million people could suffer envenoming annually.

items.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock
items.summary: Israel's election has ended in a deadlock, with neither side able to claim a majority after about 90% of votes were counted.

items.title: Clinicians warn GLP-1 drugs could worsen rising eating disorders
items.summary: Some clinical psychologists say GLP-1 weight-loss drugs can be a potential trigger for eating disorders. A new report suggests the global incidence of conditions including anorexia nervosa is rising.

items.title: Research finds nearly 2 in 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots
items.summary: New research shows that nearly two out of three teens and tweens use AI chatbots.

items.title: Indian AI firm reportedly seeks $3 billion in debt for Nvidia chips
items.summary: An Indian AI infrastructure firm is reportedly seeking to raise $3 billion of debt to buy Nvidia's next-generation chips.

items.title: Astronauts install new solar array on the International Space Station
items.summary: Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the ISS. Once the final array is installed on Nov. 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power.

items.title: T&T men qualify for FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup 2026 main draw
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago's men completed the FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup 2026 main draw, along with the Cuba women and Dominican Republic.

items.title: Astronomers resolve 170-year-old wobble in a two-star system 16 light-years away
items.summary: Astronomers found that a wobble in a nearby two-star system was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet. Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, but smaller, potentially habitable planets may remain.

items.title: Seahorse-like deep-sea fish found to be a separate evolutionary group
items.summary: Scientists found that three deep-sea fish nicknamed 'sea muppets' look like seahorses but belong to a separate evolutionary group, showing the body shape evolved more than once.

items.title: Erin Patterson loses appeal against mushroom murder convictions
items.summary: Three Australian appeal judges dismissed all seven grounds on which Erin Patterson argued her trial was unfair, leaving her convictions in place.

items.title: Chronic back pain may be tied to the brain's sense of identity
items.summary: UC San Diego researchers found that movement-triggered pain in people with chronic lower back pain activates a brain network associated with self-awareness and memories.

items.title: Canada and EU launch alliance covering Ukraine, minerals and AI
items.summary: Canada and the European Union launched a new alliance with deals on Ukraine, minerals and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Driver won't face charges in death of San Francisco GLIDE worker
items.summary: A driver will not face charges in the death of a GLIDE worker in San Francisco.

items.title: Alcatraz closure disrupts tourists' plans
items.summary: The closure of Alcatraz has disrupted tourists' plans. The island is scheduled to reopen Nov. 18, though that could be extended due to bad weather.

items.title: Church of Scientology to buy Financial District building
items.summary: The Church of Scientology plans to expand its San Francisco operations by purchasing a building in the Financial District.

items.title: Scientists investigate deaths of more than 500 penguins in Antarctica
items.summary: More than 500 penguins died on Antarctica's Danger Islands. Avian flu was the prime suspect, but researchers were surprised by what they found.

items.title: Candidates for San Francisco's District 8 seat profiled
items.summary: Mission Local profiled the candidates running in San Francisco's District 8.

items.title: US and Japan agree on Japanese facility for joint missile production
items.summary: The US and Japan announced Wednesday that they will establish a facility in Japan for joint missile production. The allies have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

items.title: China elevates a military general to the Politburo
items.summary: China elevated a military general to the Politburo and moved to strengthen party discipline. The change comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure a fourth five-year term.

items.title: T&T hosts business trade and investment talks with Venezuela
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago hosted business-to-business trade and investment talks with Venezuela.

items.title: Weakened brain signal may link several schizophrenia symptoms
items.summary: Scientists identified a weakened brain signal that may connect several symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech and greater symptom severity.

items.title: Study links six sugar substitutes to faster cognitive decline
items.summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that those consuming the most artificial sweeteners had a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to about 1.6 additional years of brain aging.

items.title: 700,000-year-old elephant tooth found alongside stone tools in Israel
items.summary: A preserved tooth from a straight-tusked elephant, dating back nearly 700,000 years, was discovered in northern Israel alongside ancient stone tools. It points to a lush environment shared by giant elephants and early humans.

items.title: Juno finds Jupiter's solar wind defenses are more complex than Earth's
items.summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft found that Jupiter uses a complex system of plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind, revealing major differences from Earth.

items.title: Mathematicians argue cosmic expansion model is unstable, questioning dark energy
items.summary: Mathematicians say they have found a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe. Their calculations suggest the framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable, which could challenge the need for dark energy.

items.title: Daytime bright light exposure linked to lower dementia risk
items.summary: In a study of more than 87,000 adults, higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia. Fewer than 42 minutes of bright daylight was linked to higher risk.

items.title: AI-powered drones are being used by both sides in the Ukraine war
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine both use drones powered by artificial intelligence, which is making them faster and more capable. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead battlefield decisions as soon as next year.

items.title: Ice in Tibet may be more than 128,000 years old
items.summary: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet may be more than 128,000 years old, preserving a record of Earth's climate that scientists thought had been lost.

items.title: Biologists probe how spider silk proteins form a strong fiber
items.summary: By probing its molecular structure, biologists are uncovering how a tangle of unstructured proteins turns into strong, flexible spider silk.
